Jan Frylinck | Player of the Match: (On his feelings) Yeah, really good. I just felt better putting a unit back that up from the previous game, which is good to see. (On his batting and support from the other batters) Yeah, I would say so. But we're just targeting big partnerships and trying to take it deep and get every set batter at the end, so we can take the bowlers down. (On his great run of form) Yeah, it's obviously very nice, but we still have two games to go, two big ones. So just looking forward to that.

Lorcan Tucker | Ireland Stand-in Captain (1/1): (On falling 63 runs short today) I think Namibia were probably better than us for large parts of the game. I think we scrapped hard. We tried to build partnerships that weren't quite successful. I think with the ball, we couldn't quite build the pressure we needed to. They came home really strong. Jan scored a brilliant hundred. I think with the top order with the bat, we didn't quite set the game up for Curtis like we should have. He played absolutely exceptionally. But yeah, we left him with too much to do. (On the areas they did well apart from Curtis' batting) I thought we bowled well in the powerplay. I thought we scrapped hard at the end. I think they played really well. They had some good power hitting. But I thought we tried to shut them down and kept them to a reasonable total.

Tucker (2/2): I thought we got through the powerplay okay ourselves. It was just that little period afterwards where we lost three wickets. It's hard to chase a score of 320 when you're losing three wickets in the space of a couple of overs to really build on that. So yeah, that was probably our downfall. (On the next game being a must-win encounter for them) Yeah, it's been a great series so far. Obviously, we've gone 1-0 up, but Namibia have come back strongly. Those are the ebbs and flows of the game. I think we just try to take as much information from these games as we can and try to implement it. But yeah, I think we have work to do, and hopefully we can do it.

Gerhard Erasmus | Namibia Captain (1/1): (On two good wins on the trot) Yeah, I think what leadership strive for is consistency. So it's a nice trajectory, as you say, and hopefully in a couple of days' time we can do it again, obviously. But yeah, it's going to be a new game of cricket again. I just thought the boys really recovered well after the previous game. We sort of historically had our first win against a Test country, but we felt that it wasn't really our best in terms of the fielding and bowling performance in the previous game. So we had some stern chats, and I think today's was almost, again, a very clinical performance. A couple of glimpses of the previous games in the end again, but yeah, it's something that we know we can tick off the drawing board if we can do that well in the next game.

Erasmus (2/2): (On the lively fielding and the run-outs today) Yeah, excellent run-out. Also, the previous game had an excellent run-out. So if big moments like that can go your way, and fielders with real determination and guys who bring you that culture in the field of not giving up, it's usually those fit guys like Malan who tend to change the game. We've had big games in the past as well where he's done that. And I think those moments in cricket aren't always as highly celebrated as hundreds and stuff. But if they win you cricket games, then I think they're just as valuable.

Namibia will be mighty pleased with their brilliant performance in all aspects of the game today. These two wins on the trot definitely show the hard work they have put in behind the scenes. Ireland, meanwhile, are under the pump. They haven't lived up to expectations so far in the series. With the series on the line, the visitors need a swift turnaround if they are to stop this talented Namibian side in home conditions. Join us for the 4th ODI in a couple of days.
